thread:
Maria (Docs): hey team — opened a small PR with examples for audit log redaction + a Ruby SDK export snippet. trying to make the SOC2 wording clear and GDPR-friendly. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4122 :wave:
Sam (Security): thanks — quick look. main ask: avoid 'irreversible' unless we can prove it. prefer 'pseudonymize' or 'mask' depending on whether the original can be recovered. also make TTL examples explicit (e.g. 30d) so customers know unit semantics.
Julian (Legal): +1 on not using 'irreversible'. for EU wording we should prefer the term "pseudonymization" (GDPR art.4) and call out when a mapping key exists. if no mapping exists, say 'redacted and not recoverable by Redwood'.
Maria (Docs): noted. current draft has both 'redaction' and 'de-identification' used interchangeably — I'll standardize to 'pseudonymization' and add a short parenthetical for 'masking (reversible) vs pseudonymization (irreversible to us)'.
Aaron (Eng): sample Ruby SDK snippet looks fine but the CLI example uses `--deid` flag name which doesn't match the SDK param `deidentify:true`. i'll push a tiny change to make names line up.
Maria (Docs): dropping the snippet here for quick eyeballs — please nit:

```json
{
  "event_type": "file.download",
  "user": "user_abc123",
  "tenant_id": null,
  "file": {
    "name": "payments.csv",
    "redacted_fields": ["cc_number", "ssn"]
  },
  "retention": "30d",
  "pseudonymization": "applied"
}
```

Maria (Docs): and the Ruby SDK example I plan to land: 

```ruby
client = Redwood::Client.new(api_key: ENV['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
client.exports.create(
  tenant: 'tenant-123',
  scope: 'audit_logs',
  retention_days: 30,
  pseudonymize: true
)
```

Sam (Security): couple tiny things: in the JSON sample, set `tenant_id` to "tenant-123" for the primary example, then add a second short example showing `null` for tenant-rehoming edge-case. and rename `pseudonymization` to `pseudonymize: "true|false"`? or keep boolean `pseudonymize: true`. boolean is better.
Julian (Legal): for the human-facing doc copy, suggest this sentence: "We pseudonymize customer data in audit exports where requested; where pseudonymization is not possible, we redact fields and document the limitations." also add a one-line footnote: "Pseudonymization does not necessarily mean data is irreversibly destroyed."
DocsBot: link-checker: found 1 broken link in PR -> docs/reference/exports.md#cli-usage (404). please update to /docs/reference/exports/cli.md or add redirect.
Maria (Docs): thanks @DocsBot — i'll fix the link in this PR.
Aaron (Eng): i'll update the SDK param to `pseudonymize: true` and add the `--pseudonymize` CLI flag alias for parity. will send a runtime patch for the CLI help text so docs and CLI match.
Maria (Docs): legal sign-off needed on final sentence. @Julian can you approve the wording above or propose final tweak?
Julian (Legal): approve with that footnote added. also please remove phrasing like 'we permanently remove' unless we mean permanent deletion. prefer 'we remove from active export datasets' or similar.
Maria (Docs): great — i'll make the changes and ping once pushed. planning to land after Aaron's small param rename and DocsBot link fix check. thanks all :heart:
Sam (Security): 👍 once changed i'll do a final security quick-pass (5 min).
Aaron (Eng): will ping here when the SDK/CLI patch is merged.
Maria (Docs): cool — target to merge today. tagging final checklist: 1) standardize terms to 'pseudonymize' 2) add TTL example formats (30d / 90d) 3) add JSON edge-case with tenant_id null 4) fix docs link 5) legal footnote.
Sam (Security): looks good.
Maria (Docs): thanks — closing thread when merged :white_check_mark:
